headline: Morocco Rejects Fuel Profit Caps to Avoid Subsidy Costs
summary: The Moroccan government has ruled out capping fuel company profits, citing that a return to subsidies could cost the state approximately $7.2 billion.
why: Fuel pricing policies in emerging markets significantly impact fiscal budgets and inflation, directly affecting the profitability of energy distributors.

impacts.name: Energy
impacts.why: Avoiding price caps preserves profit margins for fuel retailers.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: The decision prevents a regulatory squeeze on fuel retailers, maintaining their current pricing power.
